name: vertex-abap
description: Standalone AI Code Agent for local Git projects in any language, plus SAP ABAP tools: file review and builds, serverless ABAP execution, visual debugger, code and data explorers, and MCP for AI assistants

commands.title: VERTEX: Add the VERTEX MCP server to Claude Code or Codex

vertex.mcp.port.markdownDescription:
[Add the VERTEX MCP server to Claude Code or Codex](command:vertex.mcpAddress) - copies what to paste: a command for Claude Code, a config section for Codex. Copilot finds the server by itself.

Local MCP port for Codex, Claude Code and Copilot. Reload the window after changing it. Use a different port for each simultaneous VERTEX window; 0 selects a temporary port. The bearer token is kept in VS Code SecretStorage.

vertex.chat.mcpServer.markdownDescription: Where the VERTEX chat's SAP tools come from: `VERTEX` (its own tools) or the `name` of a server in `#vertex.chat.mcpServers#`. Picked in the VERTEX panel, beside the SAP system. The debugger and ABAP transpiler tools stay VERTEX's either way.

vertex.chat.orchestratorProvider.markdownDescription: Planning provider used only in **VERTEX Orchestrator**. Prepares a plan and context before the chat model executes the task. Empty disables planning. Choose provider and model with **VERTEX: Configure Orchestrator Planner**.

vertex.chat.orchestratorModel.markdownDescription: Exact model ID for the orchestrator planner. Independent of the executor model selected in the chat. Configure with **VERTEX: Configure Orchestrator Planner**.

vertex.chat.orchestratorEffort.description: Reasoning effort for the orchestrator planner, independent of the executor effort.

vertex.chat.mcpServers.markdownDescription: MCP servers the VERTEX chat can take its SAP tools from. Each is started over stdio with `command` and `args`; `env` values may use `${sapUrl}`, `${sapUser}`, `${sapPassword}`, `${sapClient}`, `${sapInsecure}` (`true`/`false`), `${tlsRejectUnauthorized}` (`0`/`1`) from the active SAP system, `${arc1AllowWrites}`, `${arc1AllowTransportWrites}`, `${arc1AllowedPackages}`, `${arc1AllowDataPreview}`, `${arc1AllowFreeSql}`, `${arc1AllowGitWrites}` from `#vertex.chat.arc1Access#`, `${abapAdtPackage}` from `#vertex.chat.abapAdtAccess#`, `${vspReadOnly}` and `${vspTransports}` from `#vertex.chat.vspAccess#`, and `${vspPath}` (usable as `command`) from `#vertex.chat.vspPath#`. `download` names where to get a command that is not found. An entry with `url` instead of `command` is a server that already runs and is reached over Streamable HTTP, such as SAP's ADT MCP Server; its `url` and `headers` may use `${adtMcpPort}` and `${adtMcpToken}` from SAP's `adt.mcpServer` settings, and `notRunning` says what to switch on when nothing answers. For a server that reads its connection only from a file, `envFile` lists the lines of a temporary `.env` that VERTEX writes in its own storage while the server runs and deletes when it stops; `${envFile}` in `args` is that file's path. The password comes from the OS credential store and is never written to settings; it is on disk only in that temporary file. `npx` needs Node.js installed.

description.description: What the server is for and what it is strong at, in two or three sentences. The VERTEX Orchestrator shows it to the model in its catalog, and VERTEX: MCP Servers shows it to you.

download.description: Where to get the command when it is not found; shown in the error.

url.description: For a server that already runs and is reached over Streamable HTTP, instead of command.

notRunning.description: What to switch on when nothing answers at url; shown in the error.

note.description: What the model should know about this server; added to its instructions.

default.name: ARC-1
default.description: Nine broad tools (SAPRead, SAPSearch, SAPNavigate, SAPContext, SAPLint, SAPDiagnose, SAPManage, SAPTransport, SAPGit), each with several actions. Strong at understanding an object with its dependency contracts, local abaplint checks, system capability probes and abapGit; writes are gated by package and by what vertex.chat.arc1Access allows.

default.name: mcp-abap-adt
default.description: Over 250 narrow ADT tools, one per object type and operation: read, create, change, delete, activate and syntax-check classes, programs, function modules, DDIC, CDS and RAP objects; versions and diffs; ABAP Unit and ATC; transports; table contents and SQL; profiler traces and dumps; the ABAP and AMDP debugger. The read-only package serves only the reading tools.

default.name: vibing-steampunk
default.description: One SAP tool with actions (read, edit, create, delete, search, query, grep, test, analyze, debug, rfc, revisions, lint). Strong at editing a single method with automatic lock and activation, package boundary analysis, and calling RFC function modules through the classic gateway.

default.name: SAP ADT
default.description: SAP's own MCP server inside ABAP Development Tools for VS Code; works on the systems logged on there. Strong at RAP: generators that create table, CDS view, behavior definition, service definition and binding in one go, publishing service bindings, and object actions as ADT offers them.
default.notRunning: It is the MCP server of SAP's ABAP Development Tools for VS Code: install that extension, set adt.mcpServer.enabled, log on to a system there, and allow that system in adt.mcpServer.accessRestrictions.
default.note: SAP ADT names a system by its destination id as SAP's ABAP Development Tools show it, such as A4H_001_DEVELOPER_EN_1 - never the bare system id. Call abap_destination_list first and pass that exact id as destination in every call. "Destination access denied" for an id that abap_destination_list did not return means a wrong id, not a missing permission.

vertex.chat.toolsets.markdownDescription: Toolsets the VERTEX chat may add on demand: a few tools of another MCP server from `#vertex.chat.mcpServers#`, offered to the model through one small `enable_toolset` tool and added only when it asks for them, so questions that need none do not carry that server's tool descriptions. An enabled toolset stays for the session. Each has a `name`, the `server`, a short `description` for the model, `tools` (names, `*` and `?` allowed) and an optional `note` the model reads when it enables the set. The default adds SAP's RAP generators and service-binding tools from the SAP ADT server, which works on the systems logged on in SAP's ABAP Development Tools.

always.description: Offer this toolset with every chosen server, not only in the VERTEX Orchestrator.

default.name: SAP RAP
default.description: Generates a RAP application (table, CDS view, behavior definition, service definition and binding) in one go, publishes service bindings and shows their OData details, and runs the actions ADT offers on an object.
default.note: SAP ADT works on the systems logged on in SAP's ABAP Development Tools, which may differ from the system VERTEX's own tools read: call abap_destination_list first, name the destination in every call, and tell the user which system was changed.

default.name: ADT: read objects
default.description: Read the source and metadata of classes, programs, includes, interfaces, function groups and modules, DDIC, CDS, RAP objects, message classes, packages and transactions.

default.name: ADT: search and where-used
default.description: Find objects and source text, where-used lists, and the ABAP syntax tree and semantic analysis of a source.

default.name: ADT: versions
default.description: Version history of an object, the source of a version and the diff between versions.

default.name: ADT: data and SQL
default.description: Table contents and free SQL queries.

default.name: ADT: change code
default.description: Create, change, delete, check and activate classes (with local types and test classes), programs, includes, interfaces, function groups and modules.

default.name: ADT: change DDIC and CDS
default.description: Create, change, delete, check and activate tables, structures, data elements, domains, table types, CDS views and message classes.

default.name: ADT: change RAP
default.description: Create, change, delete, check and activate behavior definitions and implementations, metadata extensions, service definitions and bindings.

default.name: ADT: packages
default.description: Create, change, delete and check packages and read their contents.

default.name: ADT: tests and checks
default.description: ABAP Unit and CDS unit tests (create, change, run, results), ATC runs and findings, syntax checks.

default.name: ADT: transports
default.description: Read, create and change transport requests and tasks, their objects and action log.

default.name: ADT: run and runtime analysis
default.description: Run a class or program, background runs, profiler traces, short dumps, feeds, system messages and the gateway error log.

default.name: ADT: debugger
default.description: The ABAP and AMDP debugger: listener, breakpoints, watchpoints, stepping, stack, variables and memory snapshots.

vertex.chat.mcpVersions.markdownDescription: Versions of MCP server npm packages that replace the ones named in `#vertex.chat.mcpServers#` (and `${abapAdtPackage}`), such as `{ "arc-1": "1.11.0" }`. Written by **Update** in VERTEX: MCP Servers, which appears when npm has a newer version.

enumDescriptions: Reads only: no writes, no transports.
Everything: writes in any package, transport changes, table preview, free SQL and Git writes.
vertex.chat.arc1Access.markdownDescription: What ARC-1 may do in SAP when it supplies the chat's tools. Table preview, free SQL and Git writes are on only with `write`. Also asked in the window that opens when ARC-1 is chosen in the VERTEX panel.

enumDescriptions: Reads only: runs @mcp-abap-adt/core-ro, which has no write tools.
Create, change and activate objects: runs @mcp-abap-adt/core.
vertex.chat.abapAdtAccess.markdownDescription: What mcp-abap-adt may change in SAP when it supplies the chat's tools; `${abapAdtPackage}` is the npm package that choice runs. Also asked in the window that opens when mcp-abap-adt is chosen in the VERTEX panel.

vertex.chat.vspPath.markdownDescription: The vibing-steampunk executable: `vsp` when its folder is on PATH, otherwise the file's full path (for example `C:\tools\vsp.exe`). Get it from [its releases](https://github.com/oisee/vibing-steampunk/releases); VERTEX does not download it.

enumDescriptions: Reads only: vsp refuses every write (SAP_READ_ONLY=true).
Everything: create, change, delete, activate and transports (SAP_ENABLE_TRANSPORTS=true).
vertex.chat.vspAccess.markdownDescription: What vibing-steampunk (vsp) may change in SAP when it supplies the chat's tools; passed as `${vspReadOnly}` and `${vspTransports}`. Also asked in the window that opens when vibing-steampunk is chosen in the VERTEX panel.

vertex.systems.markdownDescription:
The ABAP systems this extension can read. One of them is active at a time - see `vertex.active`, or the **VERTEX: Switch System** command.

[SAP Systems table](command:vertex.openSystemSettings) · [Import from SAP Logon and Eclipse](command:vertex.importSystems) · [Remove configured systems](command:vertex.removeSystems) · [Test the connections](command:vertex.testSystems)

Import reads each system's host and instance from SAP Logon, the client and user from an Eclipse ADT workspace, and looks for the ADT address on the usual ports. A direct SAP Logon SNC entry also supplies its SNC name, protection level and RFC server. The HTTP(S) port is also in SMICM > Goto > Services.

For SNC, use authType snc with snc and rfc.

name.description: How this system is called in the switch list.

disabled.description: Switched off: kept here, but left out of every system list, switch and test, and not connected to.

url.markdownDescription: Base URL, for example `https://host.example.com:44300`. This is the ICM port, not the one SAP GUI connects to.

client.description: SAP client, sent as sap-client. Leave empty to use the system default. With `clients`, this is the default one.

clients.markdownDescription: The clients of this system, for one user: `["600", "610"]`. The default is `client`; the SAP Systems table has a list to switch between them. Each client keeps its own password.

user.description: SAP user. For basic, the logon user — its password is asked once and kept in the OS credential store. For snc, the ABAP user the debugger targets; no password.

authType.description: Authentication type. basic uses a password; snc uses Secure Login Client over RFC. Never put a password in settings.

snc.description: SNC settings, required for snc authentication.

partnerName.description: Required. The system's SNC name, for example p:CN=SID, O=ACME.

library.description: Optional SNC library path; discovered when absent.

rfc.description: RFC address, required for snc; never derived from url. Either an application server (ashost, sysnr) or a message server with its logon group (mshost, sysid, group), as in SAP Logon.

ashost.description: Application server host. Required unless mshost is given.

mshost.description: Message server host: RFC logs on to a server of the logon group, as SAP Logon does for a group entry. Used instead of ashost.

sysid.description: System ID (e.g. PRD). Required with mshost.

group.description: Logon group with mshost. Default PUBLIC.

msserv.description: Message server port or service (e.g. 3600 or sapmsPRD). Optional; without it the SDK uses sapms<sysid>.

webgui.markdownDescription: Optional. Where the debugger opens WebGUI for this system, for example `https://10.0.0.5:44300`, when it is not `url`. Needed when SAP redirects WebGUI to a host name this computer cannot resolve.

allowInsecureCertificate.markdownDescription: Accept a server certificate that cannot be verified. Development systems often have one. **Off by default on purpose** - turning it on disables certificate checking for requests to this system.

vertex.active.markdownDescription: Which of `vertex.systems` to read from. Empty means the first one.

vertex.rfc.maxAnalysedLines.markdownDescription: RFC (SNC) systems only: the longest source, in lines, sent to SAP for hover and navigation. A longer source is not sent; double-click and F12 then find the name with abaplint inside that source. An object whose source made SAP dump is not sent again until the window is reloaded. `0` means no limit.

vertex.pathToLine.methodRelativeLines.markdownDescription: Path to line numbers lines from the method's `METHOD` statement (line 1), as SAP GUI numbers a method, instead of from the start of the source.

vertex.ai.provider.markdownDescription: AI provider used by the VERTEX assistant. API keys are kept in SecretStorage.

vertex.git.hiddenExtensions.markdownDescription: File extensions left out of the **Uncommitted changes** page and of the AI commit message request until their toggle is switched on. The commit still includes them. Can be set per workspace or folder.

vertex.ai.lmstudioUrl.markdownDescription: Address of the LM Studio local server (OpenAI-compatible). Empty uses `http://localhost:1234/v1`.

vertex.ai.ollamaUrl.markdownDescription: Address of the Ollama local server (OpenAI-compatible). Empty uses `http://localhost:11434/v1`.

vertex.ai.model.markdownDescription: Model passed to the selected provider. Empty uses the first enabled model.

vertex.ai.claudeSource.markdownDescription: Claude Code installation used by VERTEX. `ask` prompts once when both the VS Code extension and standalone CLI are available. Change this setting to switch installations.

vertex.ai.showCodemieCost.markdownDescription: Show the cost of each EPAM CodeMie answer after its token counts in the VERTEX panel. The figure is Claude Code's estimate from the model's list price, not what CodeMie charges; the budget and spending are on the CodeMie site.

vertex.ai.codemieProfile.markdownDescription: EPAM CodeMie profile used by the VERTEX assistant, as `codemie setup` named it. Empty uses the profile active in the CodeMie CLI. Chosen in **LLM Providers**.

vertex.ai.codexSource.markdownDescription: Codex installation used by VERTEX. `ask` prompts once when both the VS Code extension and a CLI are available, including the CLI inside ChatGPT.app on macOS. Change this setting to switch installations.

vertex.ai.modelConfig.markdownDescription: Which models VERTEX offers per provider (`claude`, `codex`, `copilot`, `codemie` and API providers): `hidden` model ids are left out of every model list, `versions` are Claude models checked by full id, `off: true` leaves the provider out of every provider choice. Edited with **Config models** in the VERTEX panel.

vertex.transpiler.runPath.markdownDescription: Folder that keeps each transpiler run of the chat as a folder of its own: its record, output and the sources it stepped through. A kept run opens again after a restart, from a chat citation or with **VERTEX: Open Transpiler Run...**, and its folder can be handed to someone else. Empty uses VERTEX's extension storage.

vertex.debug.runPath.markdownDescription: Folder for saved SAP debug recordings. Empty uses VERTEX's extension storage. Open the searchable run list with **VERTEX: SAP & Transpiler Logs**.

vertex.ai.logPath.markdownDescription: [Choose folder](command:vertex.ai.chooseLogFolder) for an Anthropic-compatible log (`claude_compatible/*.jsonl`). Each direct API or VS Code model call is recorded; CLI subscriptions are logged per VERTEX invocation. The checkboxes below control retained content. Empty turns logging off.

vertex.ai.log.questions.markdownDescription: Log the text of your chat questions.

vertex.ai.log.answers.markdownDescription: Log the text of the assistant's answers.

vertex.ai.log.tools.markdownDescription: Log tool calls, source-free arguments, result summaries and links to ABAP objects and recorded runs.

vertex.ai.log.toolResults.markdownDescription: With **Log tools**: also log what each VERTEX or MCP tool returned to the model - rows, search hits, messages - instead of only its size. Program source is replaced with object references; a result longer than 20,000 characters is cut, with the count of what was left out.

vertex.ai.log.localCode.markdownDescription: With **Log tools**: also log the text of the Code Agent's changes to local project files (Edit and Write), each with a link to the file. Program source from SAP is never logged.

vertex.ai.log.request.markdownDescription: Log VERTEX instructions, model context, UML and metrics snapshots, tool definitions and answer schema. Program source is replaced with object references. May contain conversation history and local paths. Applies only to new requests; provider-internal instructions are not available to VERTEX.

vertex.ai.personalInstructions.markdownDescription: Let Claude Code load your personal CLAUDE.md and auto-memory for VERTEX requests. Off by default: they travel with every SAP request and can show up in answers.

vertex.ai.effort.markdownDescription: How much the model thinks before it answers - the **Effort** list beside the model in the VERTEX panel. Claude Code and EPAM CodeMie take low, medium, high, xhigh and max (`--effort`); Codex takes minimal, low, medium and high (`model_reasoning_effort`). Empty is the assistant's own default; a level the chosen assistant does not take is not passed. API providers and GitHub Copilot do not use it.

vertex.ai.buildCommand.markdownDescription: The command that builds or tests this folder's project after the Code Agent's changes are applied (for example `npm test`, `mvn -q package`, `./build.ps1`). VERTEX runs it in the folder after **Apply** and sends a failure's output back to the assistant. Set by **Run & remember** in the review, or by hand per folder. On Windows it runs in PowerShell.

vertex.ai.shellWithoutAsking.markdownDescription: Run the Code Agent's shell commands in its git working copy without asking. Off by default. The working copy keeps file changes for review, but a command can still reach outside it: an absolute path into your folder, git commands on the shared repository (commit, branch, reset, stash, push), the network. A folder outside git always asks.

enumDescriptions: SAP's ZAVE_REVIEW table, shared with AVE and every VERTEX window on that system.
A JSON file per request in the review folder.
Both: the table is read first, and every save writes both.
vertex.review.storage.markdownDescription: Where a code review is saved. The table needs VERTEX's ABAP on the system (`ZCL_VX_ADT_RES_STORE`); on a system without it reviews are saved to files only, and the review says so.

vertex.review.folder.markdownDescription: Folder for reviews saved to files, one `<system>/<request>.json` each. Empty means `.vertex/reviews` in the first workspace folder; a relative path is taken from there too.

vertex.rfcTrace.description: SAP NW RFC SDK trace for SNC connections: 0 off, 1-3 more detail. The SDK writes dev_rfc*.log into vertex.rfcTraceFolder; the SAP Systems panel opens that folder. Takes effect on the next connection.

vertex.rfcTraceFolder.description: Folder for the RFC trace files. Empty: vertex-rfc-trace in the system temporary folder.

vertex.ai.contextMode.description: Context source for the VERTEX chat. SAP uses SAP editors and VERTEX analysis/debugger views; Folder uses local project files and Git reviews. Auto initially selects from the active editor; the panel offers SAP / Folder.

editor/context.when: editorLangId == abap && (resourceScheme == vertex-sap || resourceScheme == file || resourceScheme == untitled)
editorLangId == abap && (resourceScheme == vertex-sap || resourceScheme == file || resourceScheme == untitled)

vertex.tools.context.when: resourceScheme == vertex-sap || resourceScheme == vertex-source || resourceScheme == file || webviewSection == vertex-object
resourceScheme == vertex-sap || resourceScheme == vertex-source || webviewSection == vertex-object

keybindings.when: editorTextFocus && editorLangId == abap && (resourceScheme == vertex-sap || resourceScheme == vertex-source)
